q: The Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the Railway Board is also the ex-officio ____ of the Government of India.
e: The Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the Railway Board is the administrative head of Indian Railways and also holds the post of ex-officio Principal Secretary to the Government of India in the Ministry of Railways.

q: Who was the first Chairman of the Railway Board after Independence?
e: F. C. Badhwar was appointed Chairman of the Railway Board in 1951, when the post of Chairman replaced that of Chief Commissioner, and he is recorded as the first Indian to hold the Chairmanship.

q: The registered office of the Container Corporation of India Limited (CONCOR) is located at:
e: CONCOR, the Container Corporation of India Limited under the Ministry of Railways, has its registered and corporate office at New Delhi, from where its container terminal network is administered.

q: The Konkan Railway Corporation Limited was incorporated in the year:
e: Konkan Railway Corporation Limited was incorporated in 1990 as a public sector company to build and operate the Konkan Railway line along the west coast through Maharashtra, Goa and Karnataka.

q: Chennai Metro Rail Limited (CMRL) is a joint venture of:

options.A: Government of India and Government of Karnataka
options.B: Government of Tamil Nadu and Chennai Corporation
options.C: Government of India and Government of Tamil Nadu with equal equity participation
options.D: Indian Railways and Government of Tamil Nadu

e: Chennai Metro Rail Limited is a special purpose vehicle set up as a joint venture of the Government of India and the Government of Tamil Nadu, with equal equity participation by both governments.

q: The motto of the Railway Protection Force (RPF) is:
e: The motto of the Railway Protection Force is "Yasho Labhasva", a Sanskrit phrase meaning "attain glory", which the force carries as its guiding ideal in protecting railway property and passengers.

q: The Govind Vallabh Pant Shield is awarded every year to:

options.A: The best performing zonal railway for overall efficiency
options.B: The cleanest railway station of Indian Railways
options.C: The best production unit of Indian Railways
options.D: The best railway workshop of Indian Railways

e: The Govind Vallabh Pant Shield is the Railway Board shield awarded each year to the zonal railway judged the best performing for overall efficiency among all zones of Indian Railways.

q: Which production unit became the world's largest railway coach manufacturer in 2018-19 by rolling out 3,262 coaches in a year?
e: Integral Coach Factory, Chennai rolled out 3,262 coaches in 2018-19, the highest annual output by any coach builder, making it the world's largest railway coach manufacturer that year.

q: The registered office of Burn Standard Company Limited, the wagon-building public sector undertaking, is located at:
e: Burn Standard Company Limited, the wagon-building public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Railways, has its registered office at Kolkata in West Bengal.

q: The Rail Land Development Authority (RLDA), a statutory authority under the Ministry of Railways, was set up in the year:
e: The Rail Land Development Authority, the statutory authority for commercial development of railway land, was set up under the Railways (Amendment) Act and came into existence in 2006.

q: Complaints and disputes relating to railway freight rates and the classification of goods are adjudicated by the:
e: The Railway Rates Tribunal is the specialised tribunal that adjudicates complaints and disputes about railway freight rates, reasonableness of charges and classification of goods.

q: The Central Organisation for Modernisation of Workshops (COFMOW) was created in the year:
e: The Central Organisation for Modernisation of Workshops was created in 1979 to plan and oversee the modernisation and capacity augmentation of railway workshops across Indian Railways.

q: Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL) was incorporated primarily to implement which programme of the Ministry of Railways?
e: Rail Vikas Nigam Limited was incorporated to implement the National Rail Vikas Yojana, the programme for strengthening the Golden Quadrilateral and port-connectivity rail links through extra-budgetary resources.

q: Central Railway, the first zonal railway formed after Independence, came into existence on:
e: Central Railway came into existence on 5 November 1951 by grouping the Great Indian Peninsula Railway with several other railways, and it was the first zonal railway formed after Independence.

q: The Carriage Repair Shop at Tirupati functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Carriage Repair Shop at Tirupati, which undertakes periodical overhaul of passenger coaches, is a workshop unit functioning under South Central Railway.

q: The Wagon Workshop at Guntupalli, which undertakes periodical overhaul of wagons, is located near:
e: The Wagon Workshop at Guntupalli, which carries out periodical overhaul of freight wagons, is situated near Vijayawada in Andhra Pradesh, within the Vijayawada area of South Central Railway.

q: The Zonal Railway Training Institute (ZRTI) at Bhusawal belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The Zonal Railway Training Institute at Bhusawal, which trains railway staff of the Bhusawal division area, belongs to Central Railway.

q: The Zonal Railway Training Institute (ZRTI) at Muzaffarpur functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Zonal Railway Training Institute at Muzaffarpur, serving staff training needs in the Sonpur and Samastipur region, functions under East Central Railway, headquartered at Hajipur.

q: The largest diesel locomotive shed of Indian Railways is located at:
e: The diesel locomotive shed at Visakhapatnam, with a holding capacity of over 300 locomotives, is the largest diesel locomotive shed of Indian Railways.

q: The Rail Coach Naveenikaran Karkhana (coach refurbishment factory) at Barhi near Ganaur in Sonipat district is located in the State of:
e: Barhi near Ganaur, where the Rail Coach Naveenikaran Karkhana for refurbishment of coaches has been set up, lies in Sonipat district of Haryana.

q: Mendipathar is the only railway station of which State?
e: Mendipathar in the North Garo Hills is the only railway station in Meghalaya, the State that got its first rail connection through this station on the Dudhnoi-Mendipathar line.

q: The headquarters office of Western Railway is located at:
e: The headquarters office of Western Railway is located at Churchgate in Mumbai, the historic terminus building from which the zone's administration functions.

q: Subedarganj, where the headquarters office of the North Central Railway is situated, is in which city?
e: Subedarganj, where the headquarters office of North Central Railway is situated, is a locality in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh, close to the city's main railway station.

q: India's first centralised air-conditioned railway terminal, inaugurated in June 2022 at Baiyappanahalli in Bengaluru, is the:
e: The Sir M. Visvesvaraya Terminal at Baiyappanahalli, Bengaluru, inaugurated in June 2022, is India's first centralised air-conditioned railway terminal, modelled on airport-style facilities.

q: In the passenger reservation system of Indian Railways, 'CONCERT' stands for:

options.A: Centralised Online Network for Computerised Reservation and Ticketing
options.B: Computerised Organisation for National Coach Reservation and Ticketing
options.C: Country-wide Network of Computerised Enhanced Reservation and Ticketing
options.D: Country-wide Organisation for Computerised Electronic Reservation and Ticketing

e: CONCERT is the passenger reservation software of Indian Railways, and its full form is Country-wide Network of Computerised Enhanced Reservation and Ticketing, running the PRS terminals across India.

q: In the Accounts Department of Indian Railways, 'TIA' stands for:
e: In the Accounts Department of Indian Railways, TIA stands for Travelling Inspector of Accounts, the officer who inspects station and office accounts on tour.

q: In Indian Railways, 'ISA' stands for:
e: In Indian Railways, ISA stands for Inspector of Stores Accounts, the accounts officer who verifies and inspects the accounts and stock of stores depots.

q: In Indian Railways, 'PCOM' stands for:
e: PCOM stands for Principal Chief Operations Manager, the head of the Operating Department at zonal railway headquarters, responsible for train operations.

q: In Indian Railways, 'PCCM' stands for:
e: PCCM stands for Principal Chief Commercial Manager, the head of the Commercial Department at zonal headquarters, responsible for passenger and freight commercial matters.

q: 'IREM', the codified manual governing the service conditions of railway employees, stands for:
e: IREM stands for Indian Railway Establishment Manual, the codified manual that lays down the service conditions, recruitment, promotion and allied establishment rules for railway employees.

q: In Indian Railways, 'PCPO' stands for:
e: PCPO stands for Principal Chief Personnel Officer, the head of the Personnel Department at zonal railway headquarters, dealing with human resource and establishment matters.

q: In the budget and works programme of Indian Railways, 'PH' stands for:
e: In the Railway Budget and Works Programme, PH stands for Plan Head, the classification heads under which capital and revenue works expenditure is planned and booked.

q: In the works programme of Indian Railways, 'M&P' stands for:
e: In the Works Programme of Indian Railways, M and P stands for Machinery and Plant, the Plan Head covering procurement and replacement of machinery and plant for workshops and depots.

q: In the hierarchy of the organised Group 'A' services of Indian Railways, 'SAG' stands for:
e: SAG stands for Senior Administrative Grade, the grade in the hierarchy of the organised Group A services of Indian Railways above the Selection Grade and below the Higher Administrative Grade.

q: In railway construction contracts, 'EPC' stands for:
e: In railway construction contracts, EPC stands for Engineering, Procurement and Construction, the turnkey mode in which one agency designs, procures materials and constructs the project.

q: Who became the first woman Director General of the Railway Protection Force (RPF) in 2025?
e: Sonali Mishra, an Indian Police Service officer, took charge in 2025 as Director General of the Railway Protection Force, becoming the first woman to head the RPF.

q: The Chenab Rail Bridge of the USBRL project, dedicated to the nation in June 2025, stands at a height of about ____ above the river bed.
e: The Chenab Rail Bridge of the Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link stands about 359 metres above the river bed, making it the world's highest railway arch bridge.

q: India's first RRTS 'Namo Bharat' service, inaugurated in October 2023, was launched on the priority section between:

options.D: Sarai Kale Khan and Anand Vihar

e: India's first RRTS, the Namo Bharat service inaugurated in October 2023, began on the priority section of the Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut corridor between Sahibabad and Duhai Depot.

q: The New Pamban Bridge, India's first vertical-lift railway sea bridge, was inaugurated in:
e: The New Pamban Bridge, India's first vertical-lift railway sea bridge connecting Rameswaram with the mainland, was inaugurated in April 2025.

q: The Bairabi-Sairang new railway line, inaugurated in September 2025 to connect Aizawl with the rail network, has a length of about:
e: The Bairabi-Sairang new railway line in Mizoram, inaugurated in September 2025 to bring Aizawl on the rail map, has a length of about 51.38 km.

q: With the opening of the Bairabi-Sairang line in September 2025, Aizawl became the ____ capital of a North-Eastern State to be connected by rail.
e: With the Bairabi-Sairang line, Aizawl became the fourth North-Eastern State capital connected by rail, after the capitals of Assam, Arunachal Pradesh and Tripura.

q: India's first hydrogen-powered train, which underwent load trials in 2025, has been manufactured by:
e: India's first hydrogen-powered train, which underwent load trials in 2025, has been developed and manufactured by the Integral Coach Factory at Chennai.

q: During the COVID-19 pandemic, the 'Oxygen Express' trains of Indian Railways were specially run to transport:
e: During the COVID-19 pandemic, Oxygen Express trains were run by Indian Railways to carry Liquid Medical Oxygen in cryogenic tankers from steel plants to States facing acute oxygen shortage.

q: In January 2025, India's operational metro rail network crossed the 1,000 km milestone, making it the ____ largest metro network in the world.
e: In January 2025 India's operational metro rail network crossed 1,000 km, placing the country third in the world in metro network length, behind only China and the United States.

q: The first 16-coach 'Namo Bharat Rapid Rail' service, flagged off in April 2025, runs between:
e: The first 16-coach Namo Bharat Rapid Rail service, flagged off in April 2025, runs between Jaynagar and Patna in Bihar; the earlier Ahmedabad-Bhuj service had only 12 coaches.

q: The 'Harshacharita', a biography of King Harshavardhana, was written by:
e: The Harshacharita, the biography of King Harshavardhana of Kannauj, was written by Banabhatta, the court poet of Harsha, in Sanskrit prose.

q: The famous Sanskrit play 'Mudrarakshasa', based on the court intrigues of the Mauryan age, was written by:
e: Mudrarakshasa, the Sanskrit drama on the political intrigues through which Chanakya secured the Mauryan throne for Chandragupta, was written by Vishakhadatta.

q: The famous Sufi romance 'Padmavat' was composed by:
e: Padmavat, the celebrated Sufi romance narrating the story of Padmavati and Alauddin Khalji, was composed in Awadhi by the Sufi poet Malik Muhammad Jayasi.

q: The epic poem 'Prithviraj Raso', describing the exploits of Prithviraj Chauhan, is traditionally attributed to:
e: Prithviraj Raso, the epic poem describing the exploits of the Chauhan king Prithviraj Chauhan, is traditionally attributed to his court poet Chand Bardai.

q: The 'Sur Sagar', a celebrated collection of devotional verses on Lord Krishna, was composed by:
e: Sur Sagar, the celebrated collection of devotional verses centred on the life and leelas of Lord Krishna, was composed by the blind Bhakti poet Surdas.

q: The famous treatise on mathematics, 'Lilavati', was written by:
e: Lilavati, the famous treatise dealing with arithmetic and geometry through verse problems, was written by the mathematician Bhaskaracharya, also known as Bhaskara II.

q: The celebrated work on astronomy and mathematics, 'Aryabhatiya', was written by:
e: Aryabhatiya, the celebrated work covering astronomy and mathematics including place value and planetary computation, was written by the astronomer-mathematician Aryabhata.

q: The 'Charaka Samhita', a foundational text of Ayurveda, is traditionally attributed to:
e: The Charaka Samhita, one of the foundational texts of Ayurveda dealing with internal medicine, is traditionally attributed to the sage-physician Charaka.

q: The 'Communist Manifesto' (1848) was jointly authored by:
e: The Communist Manifesto of 1848, which laid out the programme of communism, was jointly authored by Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels.

q: The political work 'Leviathan' (1651), which put forward the theory of the social contract and absolute sovereignty, was written by:
e: Leviathan of 1651, which advanced the social contract theory and justified absolute sovereignty for securing order, was written by the English philosopher Thomas Hobbes.

q: The famous work 'The Social Contract' (1762), which opens with the line that man is born free but is everywhere in chains, was written by:
e: The Social Contract of 1762, opening with the famous line that man is born free but is everywhere in chains, was written by Jean-Jacques Rousseau.

q: The satirical novella 'Candide' (1759) was written by:
e: Candide of 1759, the satirical novella mocking blind optimism through the misfortunes of its hero, was written by the French Enlightenment writer Voltaire.

q: The book 'The Selfish Gene' (1976), which popularised the gene-centred view of evolution, was written by:
e: The Selfish Gene of 1976, which popularised the gene-centred view of evolution and coined the term meme, was written by the evolutionary biologist Richard Dawkins.

q: The comic science-fiction novel 'The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy' was written by:
e: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, the comic science-fiction work that began as a radio series, was written by the English author Douglas Adams.

q: The novel 'Swami and Friends', set in the fictional town of Malgudi, was written by:
e: Swami and Friends, the novel of schoolboy Swami set in the fictional South Indian town of Malgudi, was written by R. K. Narayan, the creator of Malgudi.

q: The popular children's novella 'The Blue Umbrella', set in a small village in Himachal Pradesh, was written by:
e: The Blue Umbrella, the popular children's novella about a girl and her prized umbrella in a small Himachal Pradesh village, was written by Ruskin Bond.

q: The celebrated travel book 'The Great Railway Bazaar' (1975), an account of a long train journey across Asia, was written by:
e: The Great Railway Bazaar of 1975, the classic travel account of a four-month train journey from London across Asia and back, was written by Paul Theroux.

q: The Hunter Commission (1882) was appointed to inquire into:

options.B: The development of education, particularly primary education

e: The Hunter Commission of 1882, chaired by W. W. Hunter, was appointed to inquire into the state and development of education in India, particularly primary education.

q: The Sadler Commission (1917) was appointed to study the problems of:
e: The Sadler Commission of 1917, chaired by Michael Sadler, was appointed to study the problems and prospects of Calcutta University, though its findings influenced university education generally.

q: The Hartog Committee (1929), appointed as an auxiliary committee of the Simon Commission, reported on:
e: The Hartog Committee of 1929, an auxiliary committee of the Simon Commission chaired by Philip Hartog, reported on the growth and problems of education in British India.

q: The Butler Committee (1927) was appointed to examine:

options.A: The relations between the British Crown and the Indian princely states

e: The Butler Committee of 1927, chaired by Harcourt Butler, was appointed to examine the relations between the British Crown as paramount power and the Indian princely states.

q: The Inchcape Committee (1922-23) was appointed to suggest:

options.B: Retrenchment and economy in government expenditure

e: The Inchcape Committee of 1922-23, chaired by Lord Inchcape, was appointed to suggest retrenchment and economy in the expenditure of the Government of India.

q: The First Central Pay Commission (1946) was chaired by:
e: The First Central Pay Commission of 1946, set up to examine the pay structure of central government employees, was chaired by Srinivasa Varadachariar.

q: The First Administrative Reforms Commission (1966) was initially chaired by:
e: The First Administrative Reforms Commission of 1966 was initially chaired by Morarji Desai, who later gave up the chairmanship on becoming Deputy Prime Minister.

q: The Twelfth Finance Commission of India was chaired by:
e: The Twelfth Finance Commission, which recommended tax devolution for 2005-10, was chaired by the former RBI Governor C. Rangarajan.

q: The Thirteenth Finance Commission of India was chaired by:
e: The Thirteenth Finance Commission, which gave its recommendations for 2010-15, was chaired by the former Finance Secretary Vijay Kelkar.

q: The G. V. K. Rao Committee (1985) is associated with recommendations on:

options.C: Panchayati Raj institutions and administrative arrangements for rural development

e: The G. V. K. Rao Committee of 1985 is associated with recommendations on Panchayati Raj institutions and the administrative arrangements for rural development programmes.

q: The Committee headed by Justice B. N. Srikrishna (2017) was set up to recommend a framework for:
e: The committee headed by Justice B. N. Srikrishna in 2017 was set up by the Government of India to recommend a framework for data protection, leading to a draft data protection bill.

q: The Shaka era, which began in 78 CE and is used in the Indian national calendar, is traditionally associated with the accession of:
e: The Shaka era, beginning in 78 CE and adopted in the Indian national calendar, is traditionally associated with the accession of the Kushana emperor Kanishka.

q: The Vikram Samvat era is reckoned from:
e: The Vikram Samvat era, used in the traditional Hindu calendar, is reckoned from 57 BCE and is traditionally linked with King Vikramaditya of Ujjain.

q: The famous temples of Khajuraho in Madhya Pradesh were built by the rulers of the:
e: The temples of Khajuraho in Madhya Pradesh, famed for their Nagara architecture and sculpture, were built by the rulers of the Chandela dynasty between about 950 and 1050 CE.

q: The Dilwara Jain temples, famous for their marble carvings, are located at:
e: The Dilwara Jain temples, renowned for their intricate white marble carvings dedicated to Jain Tirthankaras, are located at Mount Abu in Rajasthan.

q: The standard meridian of India (82°30' E longitude), from which Indian Standard Time is reckoned, passes near:
e: Indian Standard Time is reckoned from the standard meridian of 82 degrees 30 minutes East longitude, which passes near Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh.

q: The Durand Line forms the boundary between:
e: The Durand Line, drawn in 1893 between Mortimer Durand and Amir Abdur Rahman Khan, forms the boundary between Afghanistan and Pakistan.

q: The currency of Indonesia is the:
e: The currency of Indonesia is the Rupiah, issued by Bank Indonesia; the Ringgit is of Malaysia and the Baht is of Thailand.

q: The capital of Switzerland is:
e: Bern is the capital of Switzerland, serving as the seat of the Swiss federal government, though Zurich and Geneva are larger and better-known cities.

q: The Parliament of Israel is known as the:
e: The Parliament of Israel is known as the Knesset, the unicameral legislature seated in Jerusalem; Diet is Japan's parliament and Majlis is used in several other countries.

q: The first woman to receive the Jnanpith Award was:
e: Ashapurna Devi, the Bengali novelist, was the first woman to receive the Jnanpith Award, honoured in 1976 for her literary contribution.

q: The youngest person to be honoured with the Bharat Ratna is:
e: Sachin Tendulkar is the youngest person honoured with the Bharat Ratna, receiving India's highest civilian award at the age of 40 in 2014.

q: Who among the following is regarded as the 'Father of Genetics'?
e: Gregor Johann Mendel is regarded as the Father of Genetics for his experiments on pea plants, which established the laws of inheritance.

q: The first recipient of the Param Vir Chakra, India's highest wartime gallantry award, was:
e: Major Somnath Sharma of the Kumaon Regiment was the first recipient of the Param Vir Chakra, awarded posthumously for his gallantry in the 1947 Battle of Badgam.

q: The headquarters of the International Cricket Council (ICC) is located at:
e: The headquarters of the International Cricket Council, the global governing body of cricket, is located at Dubai in the United Arab Emirates.

q: Which country is known as the 'Land of the Midnight Sun'?
e: Norway is known as the Land of the Midnight Sun because in its northern regions the sun does not fully set during the summer months.

q: Which country is described by the famous phrase 'the Gift of the Nile'?
e: Egypt is described as the Gift of the Nile, a phrase from Herodotus, because its civilisation and agriculture depended entirely on the Nile river in a desert land.

q: The longest river of peninsular India is the:
e: The Godavari, about 1,465 km long and called the Dakshin Ganga, is the longest river of peninsular India, ahead of the Krishna and the Narmada.

q: The corporate headquarters of the Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) is located at:
e: The corporate headquarters of the Indian Railway Finance Corporation, the financing arm of Indian Railways registered as an NBFC, is located at New Delhi.

q: The Konkan Railway Corporation Limited (KRCL) is a joint venture of the Government of India with the State Governments of:

options.A: Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu
options.D: Goa, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu

e: Konkan Railway Corporation Limited is a joint venture of the Government of India with the State Governments of Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka and Kerala, the States served by the line.

q: IRCON International Limited was originally incorporated in 1976 under the name:
e: IRCON International Limited was originally incorporated in 1976 under the name Indian Railway Construction Company Limited, before its name was shortened to Ircon International.

q: The head of the Accounts Department at a zonal railway headquarters is designated as the:

options.A: Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer

e: The head of the Accounts Department at a zonal railway headquarters is designated as the Principal Financial Adviser, the redesignated post of the former Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer.

q: The National Rail Museum at New Delhi was inaugurated in the year:
e: The National Rail Museum at Chanakyapuri, New Delhi, which preserves the heritage locomotives and coaches of Indian Railways, was inaugurated in 1977.

q: The administrative control of Braithwaite and Company Limited was transferred from the Department of Heavy Industries to the Ministry of Railways in the year:
e: The administrative control of Braithwaite and Company Limited, the wagon and structural engineering PSU, was transferred from the Department of Heavy Industries to the Ministry of Railways in 2010.

q: The headquarters of the Central Organisation for Modernisation of Workshops (COFMOW) is located at:
e: The headquarters of the Central Organisation for Modernisation of Workshops, the Railway Board organisation for workshop modernisation projects, is located at New Delhi.

q: The centralised Computer Based Test for the AFA LDCE held in 2022 was conducted by the:

options.A: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Railway Board
options.D: Director General, National Academy of Indian Railways, Vadodara

e: The centralised Computer Based Test for the AFA LDCE held in 2022 was conducted under the Director General, National Academy of Indian Railways, Vadodara, the apex training institution of the Railways.

q: The commando force of the Railway Protection Force, raised to strengthen security at railway stations and in trains, is known as:
e: CORAS, short for Commandos for Railway Safety, is the commando force of the Railway Protection Force raised to strengthen security at railway stations and in trains against terror threats.

q: The two wagon manufacturing units of Burn Standard Company Limited are located at:
e: Burn Standard Company Limited has its two wagon manufacturing units at Howrah and Burnpur, both in West Bengal, which together form its wagon-building capacity.
